history.heading: Ancient temples
paragraphs: Malta, a small archipelago in the centre of the Mediterranean, has some of the oldest free-standing stone buildings in the world: its megalithic temples, such as Ġgantija and Ħaġar Qim, date from around 3600 BCE, older than the pyramids. The Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum is an underground burial complex.

Phoenicians, Carthaginians and Romans ruled Malta. According to tradition, Saint Paul was shipwrecked there in 60 CE and brought Christianity. Arabs ruled from 870 to 1091, leaving a lasting mark on the language.

history.heading: The Knights of Malta
paragraphs: After Norman and Aragonese rule, Emperor Charles V granted Malta to the Knights Hospitaller in 1530. In the Great Siege of 1565, the Knights and Maltese defeated a massive Ottoman invasion. They then built the fortified capital, Valletta, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Napoleon expelled the Knights in 1798, and the Maltese rebelled against French rule with British help. Malta became a British colony and a key naval base. During the Second World War, it endured intense bombing, and the whole population was awarded the George Cross in 1942.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: Malta became independent on 21 September 1964, a republic in 1974, and the last British forces left in 1979. It joined the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro in 2008. The 2017 murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia led to political crisis and the prime minister's resignation in 2019.

culture.heading: Language and faith
paragraphs: Maltese, the only Semitic language written in the Latin alphabet and an official EU language, and English are official. Catholicism is deeply rooted, and village festas honouring patron saints, with fireworks and processions, are highlights of summer.
Maltese food includes pastizzi (savoury pastries), rabbit stew (stuffat tal-fenek) and ftira bread. Malta's historic sites have made it a popular filming location.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Malta is a parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the government, and the president is elected by parliament. Two parties dominate: the Labour Party and the Nationalist Party. Malta is officially neutral and is not a NATO member. Rule of law and corruption concerns have been raised by EU institutions.

economy.heading: Services economy
paragraphs: Malta has one of the fastest-growing economies in the EU. Key sectors include tourism, online gaming, financial services, shipping registration, pharmaceuticals and semiconductors. Many foreign workers have moved there, and the population has grown rapidly.
A controversial citizenship-by-investment scheme was ruled illegal by the EU Court of Justice in 2025. Housing costs, congestion and overdevelopment are concerns. The currency is the euro.
